fuente: NHC (NOAA), Tropical Weather Discussion del Pacífico este
aviso: Análisis automático del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de la NOAA (Estados Unidos). Es contexto, no un aviso oficial: la voz oficial en Ecuador es el INAMHI.
frases: La vaguada monzónica (el tramo de la ZCIT pegado al continente) pasa sobre el archipiélago, a unos 200 km al norte de Puerto Ayora, a la altura de 90° O.
Con la ZCIT tan cerca suelen aumentar los chubascos y las tormentas en las islas.
No hay ondas tropicales analizadas entre 80° y 100° O.

texto_original.zcit: The monsoon trough extends from the Pacific coast of Colombia near 05N77.5W to 01S83.5W to 02N93W. The ITCZ extends from 02N93W to 06.5N120.5W, then resumes west of a surface trough from 05.5N124.5W to 05N140W. Scattered moderate to strong convection prevails within 90 nm either side of the monsoon trough, from 03.4S to 00N between 116W and 120W, from 10N to 13N between 129W and 135.5W, and from 00N to 10N between 135.5W and 140W. ...OFFSHORE WATERS WITHIN 250 NM OF MEXICO... Surface ridging prevails across the area, with ASCAT-B and ASCAT-C scatterometer data indicating light to gentle anticyclonic winds offshore southern and southwest Mexico, and gentle to moderate mainly northern winds elsewhere. Seas are 4-6 ft offshore southern Mexico, and 5-8 ft elsewhere, except 1-3 ft in the Gulf of California. NW swell mainly contributes to these seas, except SW swell dominating over the waters offshore southern Mexico. For the forecast, a small plume of fresh to strong northerly gap winds will develop in the Gulf of Tehuantepec tonight, then pulse through Tue night. A cold front will move through the Gulf of America by mid-week, increasing and expanding these winds. Winds may reach gale-force in the Gulf of Tehuantepec late Tue night/early Wed morning, then persist to gale-force through Thu night. Fresh to near gale-force winds will then persist through at least the end of the week. Rough seas will accompany these winds, reaching 12 ft or greater by late Wed morning. Moderate or weaker winds will increase to moderate to fresh across the waters from 17N to 27N tonight due to a tightening pressure gradient, reaching strong speeds near Cabo Corrientes Mon afternoon and evening. The moderate to fresh winds will expand northward and encompass the Gulf of California and Baja California offshore waters by early Tue, then confined to from the central Gulf and Cabo San Lazaro northward by early Thu while pulsing to strong speeds. These winds should diminish by the end of the week. Meanwhile, old NW swell with seas to rough near the Revillagigedo Islands will decay tonight. Looking ahead, a new set of rough to very rough NW swell will arrive offshore Baja California Norte Wed, spreading southeast through the end of the week. ...OFFSHORE WATERS WITHIN 250 NM OF CENTRAL AMERICA, COLOMBIA, AND WITHIN 750 NM OF ECUADOR... Fresh northeast to east gap winds are ongoing in the Gulf of Papagayo per recent ASCAT scatterometer data. Moderate northerly winds are in the Gulf of Panama. Light to gentle winds prevail across the remainder of the waters. Moderate seas in mixed old, long-period SW and NW swell prevail, except for locally rough seas southwest of the Galapagos Islands. For the forecast, fresh northeast to east gap winds will pulse each night in the Gulf of Papagayo, reaching strong speeds at times, and near gale-force by the end of the week as the pressure gradient tightens. Seas will build to rough there by the end of the week. Winds will pulse to moderate to fresh in the Gulf of Panama at night through much of the week. Light to gentle winds will prevail elsewhere. Moderate to rough seas from offshore Ecuador to the Galapagos Islands will persist through the early part of the week before subsiding. Looking ahead, rough seas from an upcoming Gulf of Tehuantepec gap wind event may impact the offshore waters of Guatemala by mid-week, with moderate seas elsewhere.
